q: Glycolysis occurs in almost all living organisms. Which statement about it is best supported?
options: It occurs in the mitochondrial matrix, which explains why only eukaryotic cells are able to carry it out
It runs in the cytoplasm without O2 or organelles, suggesting it evolved very early in life's history
It occurs on the inner mitochondrial membrane and evolved only after O2 built up in the air
It occurs only in the chloroplast stroma, so it is restricted to plants and algae
explanation: Glycolytic enzymes are dissolved in the cytoplasm, so the pathway needs no membrane-bound organelles and no oxygen. It is nearly universal in prokaryotes and eukaryotes – consistent with it evolving in early anaerobic cells, before oxygen accumulated in the atmosphere. It is the shared first stage of both aerobic and anaerobic respiration.
